advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Run abort_check()/_recheck_drift before each create dispatch in reroute_ordered_create_plans (or thread make_guarded_execute) so ordered creates keep the legacy drift/lease abort guarantees.
evidence: applier.py:617 `create_tally, mutations = reroute_ordered_create_plans(...)` runs inside the try but before the guarded loop
applier.py:634-640 the loop calls `abort_check()` then `head_pin_cell[0] = _recheck_drift(...)` before each `_apply_one`
batch_dispatch.py:577 `result = _dispatch_with_backstop(batch, ctx)` — dispatches with no drift/abort recheck
batch_dispatch.py:646-659 `_dispatch_with_backstop` only re-raises fail-fast types / records backstop failures; it never calls abort_check or recheck_drift
reroute_migrated_plans preserves the guards via make_guarded_execute (batch_dispatch.py:730), but reroute_ordered_create_plans does not — an asymmetry
advisory.finding: Creates scheduled by reroute_ordered_create_plans are dispatched before the per-mutation abort_check()/_recheck_drift loop and via _dispatch_with_backstop, which performs neither check — so outbound CREATEs lose the head-drift and lost-lease abort guarantees the legacy _apply_one loop enforced on every create.
scenarios: A ref-lock heartbeat loses the lease mid-pass just as the create scheduler dispatches parent/child creates: the aborting abort_check never runs, so creates land after the lease is gone.
HEAD drifts between pin and the create dispatch: the drift is not detected until the (now create-free) legacy loop, after real vendor create calls already fired.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make reroute_ordered_create_plans reject/raise on an unexpected or missing plan disposition instead of silently bucketing it as 'deferred'.
evidence: batch_dispatch.py:557 `disposition = getattr(getattr(plan, "disposition", None), "value", None)`

batch_dispatch.py:559-560 `if disposition != "mutate": bucket = "skipped" if disposition == "noop" else "deferred"` — every non-mutate/non-noop value (including None from the getattr fallback) becomes a silent 'deferred'
A plan whose disposition attribute is absent or whose enum value is unrecognized produces the same 'deferred' outcome as a legitimately deferred plan, indistinguishable from a wiring bug
advisory.finding: reroute_ordered_create_plans classifies a plan as 'skipped' vs 'deferred' solely on disposition == 'noop' vs anything-else, and treats a missing/None disposition (getattr fallback) as 'deferred' degraded rather than surfacing an error — an unexpected disposition value is silently bucketed as deferred instead of flagged.
scenarios: A future PlanDisposition value (or a malformed plan lacking .disposition) flows through: it is silently deferred and marked degraded rather than raising, hiding the misclassification.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/assert that create-order enforcement requires ticket_plans, or surface a signal when creates are dispatched without the ordering pass.
evidence: batch_dispatch.py:534-536 `create_plans = _ordered_create_plans(ticket_plans); if not create_plans: return None, mutations`
_ordered_create_plans iterates `(ticket_plans or [])` (batch_dispatch.py:463) — a None ticket_plans yields no create plans and no ordering
The commit message asserts it 'enforce[s] that dependency order during batch apply', but callers without ticket_plans get no enforcement and no diagnostic
advisory.finding: reroute_ordered_create_plans only reorders/defers creates when ticket_plans carries dependency metadata; when ticket_plans is None (the common legacy caller) it is a pure passthrough, so the advertised parent-before-child enforcement silently does nothing on those paths with no signal that ordering was skipped.
scenarios: A caller of applier.apply that does not pass ticket_plans dispatches child creates before unbound parents exactly as before, with no defer and no warning.
